utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I look at the clock, and say a good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-04-84-R77.1, The Prosecutor versus Shefqet Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could I have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, together with Alma Imamovic-Ivanov, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you and for the Defence of Mr. Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Michael Karnavas for Mr. Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, I see that Mr. Kabashi is present in this courtroom as well. Mr. Kabashi, during the Initial Appearance on 19th of August of this year, you did not enter a plea on the counts of the indictment. Instead you chose to defer your plea, as provided for by the Rules. And it is for this purpose that the Chamber has scheduled today's hearing. Mr. Kabashi, you'll recall that at the Initial Appearance you waived your right to have the indictment read to you and that I, for the benefit of the public, read a summary. I will now read to you the charges, and then I will ask you for each charge: How do you plead? Guilty or not guilty. And your answer in reach case should be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Madam Registrar will then carefully record any pleas entered by you, Mr. Kabashi. The charges against you concern two incidents of having contumaciously failed or refused to answer questions when you appeared as a witness. I would like to invite you to stand. Mr. Kabashi, under Count 1, are you charged with contempt of the Tribunal, pursuant to 77(A)(i) and 77(G) of the Rules, committed on the 5th of June, 2007 when you appeared as a witness in the case of The Prosecutor versus Haradinaj et al. here in The Hague. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under Count 2, Mr. Kabashi, you are charged with contempt of the Tribunal, pursuant to Rules 77(A)(i) and 77(G) of the Rules, committed on the 20th of November, 2007, when you appeared as a witness in the case of The Prosecutor versus Haradinaj et al. via a video-conference link. How do you plead? Guilt or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Kabashi. Madam Registrar, would you please record that Mr. Kabashi plead guilty on both Counts. Mr. Kabashi, with regard to your guilty pleas, the Trial Chamber will further consider whether all requirements of the guilty plea are met to make a finding on your guilt. We have reserved a courtroom for this afternoon for a further hearing on this. Before we continue, could I inquire with the parties whether there is any plea agreement concluded between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There's no plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it takes two for an agreement, Mr. Karnavas, so I make take it that you are of a similar position?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I did want to point one matter which was brought to my attention by the Office of the Prosecution; that is, on the record, to inquire whether Mr. Kabashi has any objections to you sitting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll raise that matter myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Karnavas. So, therefore, perhaps you wait until what I say about it, and then, of course, can you comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just based on an assumption, let's just assume that the Chamber would accept the guilty plea and would make a finding of guilt later this afternoon, would the parties be ready to already make submissions on sentencing this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We would, Your Honours -- we were on the basis of the information that Mr. Karnavas was kind enough to provide anticipating Mr. Kabashi's pleas today. We can deal with opening the case very shortly, and any submissions on sentence which will be very straightforward. We, the Prosecution, make no submissions other than to say that any custodial sentence should reflect the gravity of the charge. We've looked at the authorities. We think it's a matter for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner, for that. May I then take it that you'll not call any further evidence in relation to sentence? Witnesses or documentary evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, could I hear your position in respect of a possible hearing of sentencing submissions later this afternoon, and, again, I cannot anticipate on the outcome of the Chamber on the acceptance of the guilty plea, but just on the basis of an assumption that, if it would be accepted, whether you'd be ready to make sentencing submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Fully ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I also then take that do you not intend to call any witnesses or to present any documentary evidence which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As far as documentary evidence, Your Honour, the only thing that I have provided thus far were the medical records. For the consideration of the Bench should they wish to review them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They have been disclosed --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- has them as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They're always copied, Your Honour. In fact, they had them before you had them. Secondly, there may be a possibility -- it's a possibility that there would one brief witness which would be the brother who would speak as a character witness; although, I have yet to make that final determination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that witness is available this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's here. He's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if would you decide to call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's here in The Hague. He's here in the Tribunal. He is the brother that came with Mr. Kabashi from New York and has been waiting for these proceedings. So it is our anticipation that we would go forward. It is rather straightforward and, of course, we would be looking forward to a final disposition today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course I cannot anticipate --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand you can't guarantee --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not only not guarantee, I cannot in any way anticipate on whether my colleagues and I would be in a position to even make up or mind today let alone to -- to pronounce a Judgement in court. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, but I just wanted to bring it to your attention so perhaps you and your colleagues will know that in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that it would -- that you would be pleased if you would know the Judgement today. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. Is there any other matter before I make a brief statement? The Prosecution or the Defence. Or you, Mr. Kabashi, would like to raise? And, again, Mr. Karnavas, that issue you touched upon already I will deal with that after I have given you an opportunity to raise any other matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no submissions thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kabashi. Nothing further. I see you're nodding no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, as announced, I will -- although that's quite unusual, I will briefly address the question of my own impartiality for the proceedings that will follow, and most likely already this afternoon. The Chamber has been made aware of the fact that the Prosecution has shared some thoughts with the Defence on potential problems with charges or challenges to the impartiality of the Judges on this Bench. Triggered by this exchange of views, which I am aware of, I decided to make the following statement. First of all, can I only speak for myself. I have considered whether I would have to recuse myself because of the initial steps taken in respect of the investigation and the prosecution of Mr. Kabashi such as issuing an order in lieu of an indictment. The Grand Chamber of the European Court on Human rights decided the case Kyprianou versus Cyprus on the 15th of December 2005. It appears from the submissions of governments that intervened in that case that the common law tradition has widely accepted a role for judges to adjudicate contempt cases if the contempt was committed in court before those same judges. The European court - and I'm now referring to the Grand Chamber - has, unlike the Chamber that first heard the application by Mr. Kyprianou, has intentionally not ruled on the compatibility of that role with the requirement of an independent and impartial court under Article 6(1) of the European Convention. It even declared it undesirable to do so. The decision on the complaint by Mr. Kyprianou was focussing very much on the circumstances of that case. And I read just two lines which may be relevant for this. The Grand Chamber said: "The present case relates to contempt in the face of the court aimed at the judges personally. They had been the direct object of the applicant's criticism as to the manner in which they conducted the proceedings." Unnecessary to emphasise that we do not find ourselves in a similar situation. In the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, more specifically, Rules 77(C) and 77(D), Judges have been given authority and responsibility to adjudicate indicate and even prosecute contempt cases very much in line with the common law tradition. I am bound by the system adopted by the Plenary of judges and I cannot decide that this system adopted by many jurisdictions and not declared inconsistent with the requirement of an impartial court, by the European Court of Human Rights, that that system should not be applied unless I would myself be convinced that I lack the required impartiality in this case. I add to this that the present case distinguishes itself from the Hartmann case in the sense that in that case the contempt charged was not contempt in the face of court but committed out of court. I further have considered that a Judge should not recuse himself, and especially not in this Tribunal where the number of Judges is limited, unless there are good reasons to do so. It is on the basis of all these considerations that I concluded that I should not recuse myself. If any of the parties would take a different position in respect of my independence and my impartiality in this case, I would expect them to make an application under Rule 15(B)(i), and I again emphasise that I have spoken for myself and not on behalf of any of my colleagues in this case. This is the statement I would like to make. Again, if I say I would expect them to make an application under Rule 15(B)(i) it would certainly be convenient to know if you are considering to make such an application in respect of me as Presiding Judge in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had we, one would have been made a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Karnavas. This concludes this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm so sorry to -- before Your Honour rises. I now it's unusual and it may be out of an overabundance of caution but if Your Honours -- Your Honour would care to address the accused, which I know is allowed, and simply get him to confirm that he takes the same view as his counsel. That he does not intend to make such an application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. While it is unusual, Mr. Kabashi, because usually counsel is speaking for you, but do you consider at any later stage to instruct counsel or even to take any initiative as to file an application for disqualification of myself or the other Judges of this Bench? Because then we would very much like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. On the contrary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. This being clarified, I think we can conclude this Status Conference. We adjourn until 2.30 this afternoon in this same courtroom. Should this change to a later time this afternoon, the Registry will immediately communicate with the parties. We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.18 p.m.
